question: According to the manual, what is the most important reason to inspect your commercial vehicle?
choice_a: Safety for yourself and other road users
choice_b: To avoid a ticket from law enforcement
choice_c: To keep the vehicle's resale value high
choice_d: To satisfy the motor carrier's paperwork requirements
explanation: The manual states, "Safety is the most important reason you inspect your vehicle, safety for yourself and for other road users."
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.1 - Why Inspect

question: What is the minimum tread depth the manual requires in every major groove on front tires?
choice_a: 2/32 inch
choice_b: 4/32 inch
choice_c: 6/32 inch
choice_d: 8/32 inch
explanation: The manual requires at least 4/32-inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires (2/32 inch on other tires).
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.3 - What to Look For (Tire Problems)

question: According to the manual, how much steering wheel play can make a vehicle hard to steer?
choice_a: More than 5 degrees
choice_b: More than 20 degrees
choice_c: More than 10 degrees
choice_d: More than 45 degrees
explanation: Steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees (about 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch steering wheel) can make it hard to steer.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.3 - What to Look For (Steering System Defects)

question: Per the manual, what happens if one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring?
choice_a: Nothing, as long as the main spring is intact
choice_b: The vehicle will pass inspection but should be watched
choice_c: The driver must reduce speed by half
choice_d: The vehicle will be put "out of service"
explanation: The manual states that if one-fourth or more of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, it will put the vehicle "out of service," though any such defect could be dangerous.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.3 - What to Look For (Suspension System Defects)

question: Which of the following is listed among the required emergency equipment a vehicle must carry?
choice_a: Three reflective triangles, or at least 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares
choice_b: A first aid kit
choice_c: A tow chain
choice_d: A spare tire iron
explanation: Required warning devices for parked vehicles include three reflective triangles, or at least 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.3 - What to Look For (Emergency Equipment)

question: According to the gauge chart in the manual, what should engine oil pressure be while the engine is idling?
choice_b: 5-20 PSI
explanation: The manual's oil pressure chart lists 5-20 PSI while idling and 35-75 PSI while operating; if pressure is low, dropping, or fluctuating, you should stop immediately.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.5 - Start Engine and Inspect Inside the Cab (Look at the Gauges)

question: When you start the engine and check the ABS indicator light on the dash, what should normally happen?
choice_a: The light stays on the whole trip
choice_b: The light never illuminates at all
choice_c: The light comes on and then turns off
choice_d: The light flashes continuously until 20 mph
explanation: The dash ABS light should come on and then turn off; if it stays on, the ABS is not working properly.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.5 - Start Engine and Inspect Inside the Cab

question: Per the manual, drivers of trucks and truck tractors transporting cargo must inspect the securement of the cargo within the first how many miles of a trip?
choice_a: 25 miles
choice_b: 100 miles
choice_c: 150 miles
choice_d: 50 miles
explanation: Drivers must inspect cargo securement within the first 50 miles of a trip and every 150 miles or three hours (whichever comes first) after that.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.6 - Inspection during a Trip

question: What is Step 1 of the seven-step vehicle inspection method described in the manual?
choice_a: Vehicle Overview, including reviewing the last vehicle inspection report
choice_b: Check engine compartment
choice_c: Start engine and inspect inside the cab
choice_d: Do a walk-around inspection
explanation: Step 1 of the seven-step method is "Vehicle Overview," which includes reviewing the last vehicle inspection report.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.1.5 - Seven-step Inspection Method

question: What does the manual recommend to avoid rolling back when starting a manual transmission vehicle?
choice_a: Rev the engine to maximum RPM first
choice_b: Partly engage the clutch before you take your right foot off the brake
choice_c: Shift directly into third gear
choice_d: Release the parking brake before applying any engine power
explanation: If you have a manual transmission vehicle, partly engage the clutch before taking your right foot off the brake to avoid rolling back.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.2.1 - Accelerating

question: How does the manual say a driver should hold the steering wheel?
choice_a: With one hand loosely on top
choice_b: With both hands close together at the top
choice_c: Firmly, with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
choice_d: With fingertips only for quick release
explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides so it won't pull away from your hands if you hit a curb or pothole.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.2.2 - Steering

question: Why does the manual recommend backing and turning toward the driver's side whenever possible?
choice_a: It is required by federal law
choice_b: It reduces wear on the tires
choice_c: It keeps the trailer brakes engaged automatically
choice_d: The driver can see better by watching the rear through the side window
explanation: Backing and turning toward the driver's side lets you watch the rear of the vehicle by looking out the side window; backing toward the right side is dangerous because you can't see as well.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.2.4 - Backing Safely

question: Before backing with a helper, what should the driver and helper agree on, according to the manual?
choice_a: A set of hand signals, including a signal for "stop"
choice_b: The exact speed of the vehicle
choice_c: Which mirror to use
choice_d: A radio frequency for communication
explanation: Before backing, work out a set of hand signals that you both understand and agree on a signal for "stop."
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.2.4 - Backing Safely (Use a Helper)

question: Most heavy vehicles with unsynchronized manual transmissions require what technique to change gears, per the manual?
choice_a: Rev-matching without the clutch
choice_b: Double clutching
choice_c: Single clutching only
choice_d: Float shifting without ever touching the clutch
explanation: Most heavy vehicles with unsynchronized manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.3.1 - Manual Transmissions

question: What does the manual instruct a driver to do before starting down a hill?
choice_a: Accelerate to build momentum
choice_b: Wait until speed builds and then downshift
choice_c: Slow down and shift down to a speed you can control without using the brakes hard
choice_d: Shift into neutral to coast
explanation: Slow down and shift down to a speed you can control without using the brakes hard before starting down a hill; otherwise the brakes can overheat and lose braking power.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.3.1 - Basic Procedures for Shifting Down

question: Why does the manual recommend downshifting before entering a curve?
choice_a: It disables the retarder automatically
choice_b: It is required so the ABS light will turn off
choice_c: It prevents the tires from ever losing traction
choice_d: It lets you use some power through the curve for stability and to speed up as you exit
explanation: Downshifting before a curve lets you use some power through the curve to help the vehicle be more stable while turning, and lets you speed up as soon as you're out of the curve.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.3.1 - Basic Procedures for Shifting Down (Before Entering a Curve)

question: According to the manual, when should a driver turn off the retarder?
choice_a: Whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered
choice_b: Only during winter months
choice_c: Only when climbing a steep upgrade
choice_d: Only when the vehicle is unloaded
explanation: Turn the retarder off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered, because when drive wheels have poor traction, the retarder may cause them to skid.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.3.4 - Retarders

question: How far ahead do most good drivers look, according to the manual?
choice_a: 5 to 8 seconds
choice_b: 12 to 15 seconds
choice_c: 20 to 25 seconds
choice_d: 8 to 10 seconds
explanation: Most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead, which is about one block at lower speeds and about a quarter mile at highway speeds.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.4.1 - Seeing Ahead

question: When should mirror adjustment be checked, according to the manual?
choice_a: Only after the first 1,000 miles of a new trailer
choice_b: Only during scheduled maintenance
choice_c: Prior to the start of any trip, when the trailer(s) are straight
choice_d: Only when the ABS light stays on
explanation: Mirror adjustment should be checked prior to the start of any trip and can only be checked accurately when the trailer(s) are straight.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.4.2 - Seeing to the Sides and Rear

question: What does the manual say about how objects appear in a convex mirror?
choice_a: They appear larger and closer than they really are
choice_b: They appear the same size and distance as in a flat mirror
choice_c: They appear inverted
choice_d: They appear smaller and farther away than they really are
explanation: Everything appears smaller in a convex mirror than it would if you were looking directly at it, and things seem farther away than they really are.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.4.2 - Seeing to the Sides and Rear (How to Use Mirrors)

question: Per the manual, besides checking mirrors before signaling a lane change, when else should you check them?
choice_a: After signaling, to check no one has moved into your blind spot, and right after starting the change to double-check your path is clear
choice_b: Only once, immediately before signaling
choice_c: Never during the maneuver itself, only afterward
choice_d: Only after you have completed the entire maneuver
explanation: Check your mirrors before changing lanes, after signaling to make sure no one has moved into your blind spot, right after you start the lane change, and after you complete it.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.4.2 - Seeing to the Sides and Rear (Special Situations)

question: What are the three good rules for using turn signals, per the manual?
choice_a: Signal loudly, signal twice, cancel immediately
choice_b: Signal early, signal continuously, cancel your signal
choice_c: Signal early, signal briefly, leave it on
choice_d: Signal only in the city, signal continuously, cancel your signal
explanation: The three rules are: signal early, signal continuously, and cancel your signal after completing the turn.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.5.1 - Signal Your Intentions (Turns)

question: If you must stop on a one-way or divided highway, at what distances should you place your warning devices?
choice_a: 10 feet, 50 feet, and 100 feet
choice_b: 5 feet, 50 feet, and 150 feet
choice_c: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet, toward the approaching traffic
choice_d: 25 feet, 75 feet, and 125 feet
explanation: On a one-way or divided highway, place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward the approaching traffic.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.5.2 - Communicating Your Presence

question: What does the manual say a driver should use, rather than just identification or clearance lights, when it's hard to see (dawn, dusk, rain, or snow)?
choice_a: Four-way flashers only
choice_b: High beams at all times
choice_c: Fog lights exclusively
choice_d: Headlights, on low beam
explanation: When it's hard to see, turn on your lights and use the headlights, not just the identification or clearance lights, using low beams since high beams can bother people even in daytime.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.5.2 - Communicating Your Presence (When It's Hard to See)

question: What does the manual advise about signaling other drivers when it's safe for them to pass?
choice_a: You should not do this, as it could cause an accident
choice_b: It's a courteous practice that should be done whenever possible
choice_c: Only bus drivers are permitted to do this
choice_d: It's required by federal law for commercial vehicles
explanation: The manual warns "Don't Direct Traffic" -- you should not signal others when it is safe to pass, because you could cause an accident and be blamed.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.5.1 - Signal Your Intentions (Don't Direct Traffic)

question: What three components make up Total Stopping Distance, according to the manual's formula?
choice_a: Reaction Distance + Braking Distance + Following Distance
choice_b: Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Braking Distance
choice_c: Perception Distance + Braking Distance + Stopping Distance
choice_d: Sight Distance + Reaction Distance + Braking Distance
explanation: The manual's formula is Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Braking Distance = Total Stopping Distance.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.6.1 - Stopping Distance

question: At 55 mph, how many feet does the manual say perception distance accounts for, given an average perception time of about 1-3/4 seconds?
choice_a: 61 feet
choice_b: 216 feet
choice_c: 142 feet
choice_d: 419 feet
explanation: The average perception time for an alert driver is about 1-3/4 seconds; at 55 mph, this accounts for 142 feet traveled.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.6.1 - Stopping Distance

question: According to the manual, what is the minimum total stopping distance at 55 mph?
choice_a: 216 feet
choice_b: 300 feet
choice_c: 350 feet
choice_d: 419 feet
explanation: At 55 mph, the vehicle will travel a minimum total stopping distance of 419 feet, combining perception, reaction, and braking distance.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.6.1 - Stopping Distance (Figure 2.11)

topic: Effect of Doubling Speed on Stopping
question: What happens to impact and braking distance when you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, per the manual?
choice_a: They become 4 times greater
choice_b: They double
choice_c: They become 9 times greater
choice_d: They stay the same
explanation: When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, the impact is 4 times greater and the braking distance is also 4 times longer.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.6.1 - Stopping Distance (Effect of Speed on Stopping Distance)

question: On a wet road, the manual recommends reducing speed by about how much compared to dry conditions?
choice_a: One-tenth
choice_b: One-third
choice_c: One-half
choice_d: Two-thirds
explanation: Reduce speed by about one-third on a wet road (for example, slow from 55 to about 35 mph); on packed snow, reduce speed by half or more.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.6.2 - Matching Speed to the Road Surface

question: What rule does the manual give for how much following distance to keep at speeds below 40 mph?
choice_a: Two seconds for every 10 feet of vehicle length
choice_b: Three seconds regardless of vehicle length
choice_c: One second for every 10 feet of vehicle length
choice_d: One second for every 20 feet of vehicle length
explanation: One good rule says you need at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.7.1 - Space Ahead

question: Per the manual's example, how many seconds of following distance should a 40-foot vehicle traveling under 40 mph leave?
choice_a: 2 seconds
choice_b: 6 seconds
choice_c: 8 seconds
choice_d: 4 seconds
explanation: If you are driving a 40-foot vehicle, you should leave 4 seconds between you and the vehicle ahead at speeds below 40 mph.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.7.1 - Space Ahead (Figure 2.12)

question: What does the manual recommend if you find yourself being tailgated?
choice_a: Increase your following distance in front of you
choice_b: Speed up to create distance
choice_c: Flash your brake lights repeatedly as a warning
choice_d: Tap your taillights on and off
explanation: If tailgated, increase your following distance to avoid sudden speed or direction changes and to make it easier for the tailgater to get around you; avoid tricks like flashing brake lights.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.7.2 - Space Behind

question: What does the manual caution about the height of a cargo van and posted bridge clearances?
choice_a: Bridge clearances never change due to weather
choice_b: An empty van is higher than a loaded one, so clearing a bridge loaded doesn't guarantee clearing it empty
choice_c: Posted bridge heights are always accurate and can be trusted fully
choice_d: Loaded vans are always taller than empty ones
explanation: The weight of a cargo van changes its height; an empty van is higher than a loaded one, so getting under a bridge loaded doesn't mean you can when empty.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.7.4 - Space Overhead

question: According to the manual, what should you make sure of before starting across a road at an intersection?
choice_a: Cross diagonally to save time
choice_b: Accelerate as fast as possible regardless of gap size
choice_c: Make sure you can get all the way across before traffic reaches you
choice_d: Always wait for a complete break in traffic in both directions simultaneously
explanation: Before you start across a road, make sure you can get all the way across before traffic reaches you.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.7.7 - Space Needed to Cross or Enter Traffic

question: How does the manual define a "hazard"?
choice_a: Only a vehicle that has already caused a crash
choice_b: Solely a mechanical defect in your own vehicle
choice_c: Any object weighing more than 50 pounds on the roadway
choice_d: Any road condition or other road user that is a possible danger
explanation: A hazard is any road condition or other road user (driver, bicyclist, pedestrian) that is a possible danger.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.8.1 - Importance of Seeing Hazards

question: Which of the following is listed as a clue to an impaired driver?
choice_a: Weaving across the road or drifting from one side to another
choice_b: Consistently signaling well in advance
choice_c: Maintaining a steady, legal speed
choice_d: Keeping windows closed in warm weather
explanation: Clues to impaired drivers include weaving across the road or drifting from one side to another, leaving the road, and stopping at the wrong time.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.8.3 - Drivers Who Are Hazards (Impaired Drivers)

question: What does the manual warn about speed limit signs posted on off ramps and on ramps?
choice_a: They are always conservative enough for any vehicle
choice_b: They may be safe for automobiles but not for larger or heavily loaded vehicles
choice_c: They apply only to passenger vehicles
choice_d: They are optional recommendations rather than requirements
explanation: Speeds posted at off ramps and on ramps may be safe for automobiles but may not be safe for larger vehicles or heavily loaded vehicles.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.8.2 - Hazardous Roads (Off Ramps/On Ramps)

question: According to the manual, why should a driver think about possible emergencies when they see a hazard?
choice_a: Because it is a legal requirement to narrate hazards aloud
choice_b: To reduce fuel consumption
choice_c: To have time to plan a way out of any emergency that develops
choice_d: To pass the vehicle inspection test
explanation: You look for hazards in order to have time to plan a way out of any emergency, making you a prepared, defensive driver.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.8.4 - Always Have a Plan

question: According to the Large Truck Crash Causation Study cited in the manual, what percentage of large-truck crashes occurred when the CMV driver was externally distracted?
choice_a: 2 percent
choice_b: 15 percent
choice_c: 23 percent
choice_d: 8 percent
explanation: The LTCCS reported that 8 percent of large-truck crashes occurred when CMV drivers were externally distracted and 2 percent occurred when the driver was internally distracted.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.9.1 - The Distracted Driving Crash Problem

question: Per the manual, dialing a mobile telephone while driving makes a CMV driver how many times more likely to be involved in a safety-critical event?
choice_a: 6 times
choice_b: 2 times
choice_c: 15 times
choice_d: 23.2 times
explanation: The odds of being involved in a safety-critical event are 6 times greater for CMV drivers who engage in dialing a mobile telephone while driving.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.9.4 - Cell/Mobile Phones

question: According to the manual, texting while driving makes a CMV driver how many times more likely to be involved in a safety-critical event than non-texting drivers?
choice_a: 6 times
choice_b: 23.2 times
choice_c: 8 times
choice_d: 12 times
explanation: Research shows the odds of a safety-critical event are 23.2 times greater for CMV drivers who engage in texting while driving.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.9.5 - Texting

question: Per the manual, how long is a CDL disqualified for a second conviction within 3 years of hand-held mobile telephone use while operating a CMV?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 90 days
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: 120 days
explanation: Disqualification is 60 days for the second offense within 3 years and 120 days for three or more offenses within 3 years.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.9.4 - Cell/Mobile Phones

question: Which of the following is listed among the manual's tips to avoid becoming a distracted driver?
choice_a: Read text messages only at stoplights
choice_b: Keep the interior cab light on for visibility
choice_c: Adjust mirrors while underway to save time
choice_d: Pre-program radio stations and pre-load favorite CDs before driving
explanation: Tips include pre-programming radio stations and pre-loading favorite CDs, adjusting mirrors before driving begins, and reviewing maps or the GPS before you start.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.9.6 - Don't Drive Distracted

question: How does the manual distinguish road rage from aggressive driving?
choice_a: Road rage involves intent to do harm or physically assault another driver or vehicle, while aggressive driving is selfish, bold, or pushy driving without regard for others' safety
choice_b: They are legally identical terms
choice_c: Aggressive driving is a crime, while road rage is not
choice_d: Road rage only applies to passenger cars, not commercial vehicles
explanation: Aggressive driving is operating a vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner without regard for others' rights or safety; road rage is operating with the intent of doing harm or physically assaulting a driver or vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.10.1 - What Is It?

question: What is the first and foremost thing the manual says to do when confronted by an aggressive driver?
choice_a: Match their speed to avoid appearing weak
choice_b: Make every attempt to get out of their way
choice_c: Flash your high beams at them
choice_d: Pull over and confront them
explanation: "First and foremost, make every attempt to get out of their way," and avoid challenging them by speeding up or holding your lane.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.10.3 - What You Should Do When Confronted by an Aggressive Driver

question: What information does the manual recommend providing when reporting an aggressive driver to authorities?
choice_a: Only the time of day
choice_b: Just a general description of "a truck"
choice_c: Vehicle description, license number, location, and direction of travel
choice_d: Nothing; you should never report aggressive drivers
explanation: Report aggressive drivers to the appropriate authorities by providing a vehicle description, license number, location, and, if possible, direction of travel.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.10.3 - What You Should Do When Confronted by an Aggressive Driver

question: How far can a vehicle travel during two seconds of glare blindness at 55 mph, per the manual?
choice_a: About a quarter of the length of a football field
choice_b: Exactly one football field
choice_c: Less than 10 feet
choice_d: More than half the distance of a football field
explanation: Even two seconds of glare blindness can be dangerous; a vehicle going 55 mph will travel more than half the distance of a football field during that time.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.11.2 - Driver Factors (Glare)

question: What does the manual say about wearing tinted or dark corrective lenses at night?
choice_a: They should be avoided because they cut down needed light for night driving
choice_b: They are recommended to reduce glare
choice_c: They are required by law after dusk
choice_d: They have no effect either way
explanation: Avoid using dark or tinted corrective lenses at night, even if you think they help with glare, because tinted lenses cut down the light you need to see clearly at night.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.11.2 - Driver Factors (Vision)

question: According to the National Sleep Foundation poll cited in the manual, what percentage of Americans admit to having fallen asleep at the wheel in the past year?
choice_a: 15 percent
choice_b: 36 percent
choice_c: 60 percent
choice_d: 100 percent
explanation: 36 percent (103 million people) admit to having actually fallen asleep at the wheel in the past year, while 60% have driven while feeling sleepy.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.11.2 - Driver Factors (Fatigue and Lack of Alertness)

question: According to the manual, roughly how far ahead can a driver see with low-beam headlights at night?
choice_a: About 100 feet
choice_b: About 350-500 feet
choice_c: About 250 feet
choice_d: About 1,000 feet
explanation: With low beams you can see ahead about 250 feet, and with high beams about 350-500 feet.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.11.4 - Vehicle Factors (Headlights)

question: Per the manual, within what distance should you dim your headlights before an oncoming vehicle or when following another vehicle?
choice_a: 100 feet
choice_b: 200 feet
choice_c: 1,000 feet
choice_d: 500 feet
explanation: Dim your lights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle within 500 feet.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.11.5 - Night Driving Procedures (Avoid Blinding Others)

topic: Best Practice for Driving in Fog
question: What is the manual's best advice for driving in fog?
choice_a: Don't drive; pull off the road until visibility improves
choice_b: Drive with high beams on at all times
choice_c: Speed up to get through the fog quickly
choice_d: Follow the taillights of the vehicle ahead closely
explanation: "The best advice for driving in fog is don't." It is preferable to pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility is better.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.12 - Driving in Fog

question: If you must drive in fog, what does the manual say about your headlights?
choice_a: Use high beams to see farther ahead
choice_b: Use low-beam headlights and fog lights for best visibility
choice_c: Turn off all lights to reduce glare
choice_d: Use only parking lights
explanation: Use low-beam headlights and fog lights for best visibility even in daytime, and turn on your four-way flashers to give vehicles behind you a quicker opportunity to notice you.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.12 - Driving in Fog

question: What does the manual recommend regarding tire chains before winter driving?
choice_a: Chains are never necessary for commercial vehicles
choice_b: Chains should only be used on the steering axle
choice_c: Learn how to put chains on before you need them in snow and ice
choice_d: Chains should be tested only at the destination
explanation: Carry the right number of chains and extra cross-links, and learn how to put chains on before you need to do it in snow and ice.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.13.1 - Vehicle Checks (Tire Chains)

question: What clue does the manual give for detecting ice on the road?
choice_a: Excessive spray from other vehicles
choice_b: A strong smell of exhaust
choice_c: The presence of tar bleeding through the pavement
choice_d: A lack of spray from other vehicles
explanation: A lack of spray from other vehicles indicates ice has formed on the road; also check your mirrors and wiper blades for ice.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.13.2 - Driving (Check for Ice)

question: Why does the manual say not to use the engine brake or speed retarder on slippery winter surfaces?
choice_a: They can cause the driving wheels to skid
choice_b: They drain the battery too quickly
choice_c: They are illegal in winter conditions
choice_d: They overheat the transmission
explanation: Don't brake any harder than necessary, and don't use the engine brake or speed retarder, because they can cause the driving wheels to skid on slippery surfaces.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.13.2 - Driving (Adjust Turning and Braking to Conditions)

question: According to the manual, what problems can wet brakes cause?
choice_a: Improved stopping power due to cooling
choice_b: Lack of braking power, wheel lockups, pulling to one side, or jackknife
choice_c: Automatic engagement of the parking brake
choice_d: No effect on braking performance
explanation: Water in the brakes can cause them to be weak, apply unevenly, or grab, causing lack of braking power, wheel lockups, pulling to one side, and jackknife if pulling a trailer.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.13.2 - Driving (Wet Brakes)

topic: Tire Inspection Interval in Hot Weather
question: How often does the manual say to inspect tires when driving in very hot weather?
choice_a: Every 30 minutes or 25 miles
choice_b: Every four hours or every 300 miles
choice_c: Every two hours or every 100 miles
choice_d: Only at the start and end of the trip
explanation: Inspect the tires every two hours or every 100 miles when driving in very hot weather.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.14.1 - Vehicle Checks (Tires)

question: What does the manual advise about letting air out of hot tires to reduce pressure?
choice_a: Do it immediately to prevent blowouts
choice_b: It has no effect on tire safety
choice_c: Only let air out if the tire is over 200 degrees
choice_d: Do not let air out, or the pressure will be too low when tires cool
explanation: Air pressure increases with temperature; do not let air out or the pressure will be too low when the tires cool off.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.14.1 - Vehicle Checks (Tires)

question: What hazard does the manual describe as "bleeding tar"?
choice_a: Tar rising to the pavement surface in hot weather, creating very slippery spots
choice_b: A tire defect caused by cold weather
choice_c: Oil leaking from the engine onto the exhaust
choice_d: A type of brake fluid contamination
explanation: Tar in the road pavement frequently rises to the surface in very hot weather, and spots where tar "bleeds" to the surface are very slippery.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.14.2 - Driving (Watch for Bleeding Tar)

question: What defines a "passive crossing" per the manual?
choice_a: A crossing with flashing lights and gates
choice_b: A crossing with no traffic control device, where the decision to stop or proceed rests entirely with the driver
choice_c: A crossing only found in rural areas
choice_d: A crossing that automatically stops all trains
explanation: A passive crossing does not have any type of traffic control device; the decision to stop or proceed rests entirely in your hands.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.15.1 - Types of Crossings

topic: Racing a Train to a Crossing
question: What does the manual say about racing a train to a crossing?
choice_a: It is acceptable if the vehicle is unloaded
choice_b: It is only dangerous at night
choice_c: Never attempt it, since it's extremely difficult to judge a train's approaching speed
choice_d: It is permitted at passive crossings only
explanation: Never attempt to race a train to a crossing; it is extremely difficult to judge the speed of an approaching train.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.15.3 - Driving Procedures (Never Race a Train to a Crossing)

question: Why does the manual say double tracks require a "double check"?
choice_a: Because signals malfunction more often on double tracks
choice_b: Because double tracks always require a full stop
choice_c: Because double tracks are only found at active crossings
choice_d: Because a train on one track may hide a train on the other track
explanation: A train on one track may hide a train on the other track; look both ways before crossing, and after one train has cleared, be sure no other trains are near before starting across.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.15.3 - Driving Procedures (Double Tracks Require a Double Check)

topic: Time to Clear a Double Track
question: Per the manual, how long does it take a typical tractor-trailer unit to clear a double track?
choice_a: More than 15 seconds
choice_b: At least 5 seconds
choice_c: At least 10 seconds
choice_d: More than 30 seconds
explanation: It takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least 14 seconds to clear a single track and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.15.5 - Crossing the Tracks

question: If a vehicle gets stuck on the tracks, what does the manual instruct the driver to do first?
choice_a: Try to push the vehicle off the tracks alone
choice_b: Get out of the vehicle and away from the tracks
choice_c: Wait inside the vehicle for the train to pass
choice_d: Honk the horn continuously until help arrives
explanation: If you get stuck on the tracks, get out of the vehicle and away from the tracks, then check for emergency notification information at the crossing and call 911.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.15.6 - Special Situations

topic: Selecting a Safe Speed on a Downgrade
question: Which factors does the manual say determine your selection of a "safe" speed for a long, steep downgrade?
choice_a: Only the posted speed limit
choice_b: Only the weight of the cargo
choice_c: Total weight of vehicle/cargo, length of grade, steepness of grade, road conditions, and weather
choice_d: Only the driver's experience level
explanation: Your most important consideration is a speed that is not too fast for the total weight of the vehicle and cargo, length of the grade, steepness of the grade, road conditions, and weather.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.16.1 - Select a "Safe" Speed

question: What does the manual warn about downshifting after your speed has already built up on a downgrade?
choice_a: It is the recommended technique for automatic transmissions
choice_b: It has no negative consequences
choice_c: It only affects fuel economy
choice_d: You may not be able to shift into a lower gear, and could lose all engine braking effect
explanation: Do not try to downshift after your speed has already built up; you may not be able to shift into a lower gear, and forcing an automatic transmission into a lower gear at high speed can damage it and cause loss of all engine braking effect.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.16.2 - Select the Right Gear before Starting Down the Grade

question: What does the manual say causes brakes to "fade"?
choice_a: Excessive heat from using the brakes too much without relying on engine braking
choice_b: Cold weather affecting brake fluid viscosity
choice_c: Using the parking brake too frequently
choice_d: Low tire pressure
explanation: Brakes can fade or fail from excessive heat caused by using them too much and not relying on the engine braking effect; brakes out of adjustment can overheat and fade even faster.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.16.3 - Brake Fading or Failure

question: What is the purpose of the escape ramps described in the manual?
choice_a: To provide a shortcut around mountain grades
choice_b: To stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers and passengers
choice_c: To allow vehicles to bypass weigh stations
choice_d: To provide additional parking on steep grades
explanation: Escape ramps use a long bed of loose, soft material to slow a runaway vehicle and are made to stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers and passengers.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.16.4 - Proper Braking Technique (Escape Ramps)
